profile.campus: Herndon, Fairfax County, Virginia (Equinix DC97, Washington DC-area IBX network)
profile.reading:
This OpenStreetMap point is labeled "Equinix DC97" at 460 Spring Park Place in Herndon, Fairfax County, Virginia, though the OSM data itself carries a "fixme: not found on website" flag left by a prior mapping contributor, and this session could not independently locate a DC97 listing on Equinix's own Washington DC-area data center pages, which run through numbered facilities including DC1 through DC22 plus a small number of specially named sites. Equinix does operate a substantial Northern Virginia and Washington DC-area IBX network anchored by its much larger Ashburn "Data Center Alley" campus in neighboring Loudoun County, where DC1 and DC2 were established in the late 1990s, so a genuine Equinix presence in the Herndon/Dulles corridor is plausible; Herndon sits directly along the same Route 28/Dulles Toll Road technology corridor as several other named Equinix and competitor facilities. Given the unresolved naming discrepancy already flagged in the source data, this registry treats "DC97" as an unconfirmed facility code rather than asserting it as an operator-verified name, and declines to assign fabricated square footage or power capacity figures rather than borrowing specifications from a different, confirmed Equinix building under this uncertain identification.

Dominion Energy, the regional utility serving most of Northern Virginia including the Herndon/Dulles corridor, has cited data center and other large-load growth as the single largest driver of new electricity demand in its Virginia service territory in filings with the Virginia State Corporation Commission, a dynamic that applies across the broader Fairfax-Loudoun data center corridor regardless of which specific operator or building code is involved.

Herndon and the surrounding Dulles corridor host a mix of colocation and network facilities from multiple operators beyond Equinix, including competitors and telecom carrier hotels, which increases the chance that a single mapped point could be mislabeled with another nearby operator's building code or an outdated internal reference; this registry treats that as the more likely explanation for the OSM fixme flag than assuming Equinix simply declined to list a real DC97 facility.

reading.body:
The facility code DC97 at 460 Spring Park Place in Herndon carries an unresolved naming discrepancy. Equinix's own Washington DC-area site listing does not include a DC97 facility code, and OpenStreetMap flagged this point as "not found on website." Equinix operates a substantial Northern Virginia IBX network anchored by its larger Ashburn campus in neighboring Loudoun County, making a genuine Equinix presence in the Herndon/Dulles corridor plausible, but this specific facility code remains unconfirmed by operator publication.

Herndon sits within Northern Virginia's data center corridor, where Dominion Energy has cited data center growth as the single largest driver of new electricity demand in its Virginia service territory. The regional context places this location along the same Route 28 and Dulles Toll Road corridor as multiple confirmed colocation and carrier facilities from several operators. Equinix has identified its Washington DC-area IBX network as a major communications gateway to Europe.

No power capacity, square footage, or infrastructure specifications are published for this facility. The unconfirmed status of the DC97 identifier means this campus cannot be ranked among Virginia's AI-relevant infrastructure at present. The next steps to resolve its role would be direct confirmation from Equinix's current IBX listing or Fairfax County property records.
